name: scoring_rules
description: Central scoring configuration. Controls how different factors contribute to job fit scoring. Must remain transparent and not contain hidden rejection logic.

calibration_notes.design: Band-anchored scoring. The LLM grade defines the band (floor/ceiling); other signals adjust the score within that band. Grade and score cannot contradict — a MISMATCH grade always produces a low score; a STRONG grade always produces a good score.
calibration_notes.llm_grade_base_points: Base additive contribution from the LLM grade before other signals are added. These are intentionally modest — the band floor and ceiling constrain the final score, not the base alone.
calibration_notes.llm_grade_bands: Each grade has a floor (minimum attainable) and ceiling (maximum attainable) for the non-hard-block score. After summing all core/preference/convenience entries the result is clamped to the band. Hard block penalties are applied after band clamping and can push the score to zero regardless of grade.
calibration_notes.other_signals: Title match, preferences, freshness, and competitive signals move the score within the grade band. Capability support is captured in the grade via requirement_coverage — it is shown for transparency but does not add separate points. A STRONG grade with a clean title and preference signals reaches the upper end of the band; the same grade with no supporting signals floors at the grade minimum.
calibration_notes.hard_blockers: Applied after band clamping. A single hard blocker subtracts 100, overriding the grade band and forcing the score to near-zero.

band_boundaries.EXCELLENT: 88-100 — reserved for exceptional alignment across all signals
band_boundaries.STRONG: 68-87 — strong fit confirmed by LLM; other signals calibrate within this range
band_boundaries.MISMATCH: 0-7 — explicit mismatch; capped near-zero regardless of other signals

fit_breakdown.description: Core score components for title fit, content fit, review status, and hard-block penalties. Internal scoring logic.

llm_grade_points.description: Base additive points for each LLM grade. These anchor the score in the correct band but are intentionally modest — supporting signals from title, capability support, and preferences move the score within the band defined by llm_grade_bands.

llm_grade_bands.description: Floor and ceiling for the non-hard-block score per LLM grade. The score is clamped to this range before hard block penalties are applied. A band adjustment entry is added to the breakdown when clamping occurs.

convergence.description: Bonuses for strong multi-signal agreement between title, content, and evidence.
convergence.label: Multiple strong signals align

competitive_signal_alignment.description: Score adjustments for competitive signals that point toward a specialist domain.

freshness.description: Bonuses for newer jobs. Used by the score engine, not the search filters. Only jobs posted within the last day receive a bonus.

work_mode.description: Score adjustment for a confirmed selected work mode. Multiple selected modes are neutral.

salary.description: Score adjustments for salary or rate fit.

location.description: Score adjustments for location fit and travel distance.

contract.description: Score adjustments for selected work-type preference, including Permanent, Contract, and FTC, plus contract-length confidence where relevant.

government.description: Score adjustments for sector matches using public-sector context evidence.

evidence_tier_weights.description: Managed defaults for profile support tier weighting. These correspond to the profile-side support weighting controls in Advanced Settings.

preference_weight_defaults.description: Managed defaults for the profile-side weight sliders shown in Advanced Settings.

deterministic_review_thresholds.description: Controls the pre-LLM deterministic shortcut in source_learning.deterministic_review_outcome. When a job clears one of these rules it is decided without an LLM call (review_source='rule'). To calibrate, filter audit_records.json on review_source='rule' or 'rule+learning' and check whether the det_rule value matches your expectation.

field_descriptions.min_high_risks_for_mismatch: Minimum missing-evidence count required to trigger a REJECT/MISMATCH when strong fit signals are absent. Raise to make the MISMATCH shortcut stricter (fewer auto-rejects).
field_descriptions.max_strong_signals_for_mismatch: Upper bound on strong fit signals for the MISMATCH rejection to fire. Lower to prevent accidental rejection of jobs that have any positive signal.
field_descriptions.min_high_risks_for_poor: Minimum missing-evidence count to auto-reject a POTENTIAL_MATCH title as POOR. Raise to keep more ambiguous titles in for LLM review.
field_descriptions.max_strong_signals_for_poor: Upper bound on strong fit signals for the POOR rejection to fire. If set too low, weak-title roles with some evidence bypass the shortcut and go to LLM.
field_descriptions.min_strong_signals_for_strong_keep: Minimum strong fit signals to shortcut to KEEP/STRONG when there are no missing-evidence items. Lower to auto-approve more confident jobs without LLM.
field_descriptions.min_strong_signals_for_solid_keep: Minimum strong fit signals to shortcut to KEEP/SOLID. Must be below min_strong_signals_for_strong_keep.
field_descriptions.max_medium_risks_for_solid_keep: Maximum soft-risk count allowed for the SOLID shortcut to fire. Raise to auto-approve jobs with more minor concerns.
